title: Lithium prices expected to rise, as demand slows down - Mining.com.au
text:
Lithium prices expected to rise, as demand slows down - Mining.com.au

- 20 August 2026
- - News

 WRITTEN BY Aaliyah Rogan 

# Lithium prices expected to rise, as demand slows down

Lithium’s price recovery is gaining firmer footing, but a wave of new supply is keeping the market from entering a full-blown bull cycle.

According to the Shanghai Metals Market (SMM), mainland Chinese lithium carbonate and lithium hydroxide monohydrate average price forecasts for 2026 have been revised up to US$20,100 ($28,218) per tonne and US$19,600 per tonne, respectively.

At the time of writing, lithium’s price stood at ¥150,000 ($31,288) per tonne in August, the highest in one month, as signs of growing demand offset the recent easing in supply, as reported by Trading Economics.

Global lithium demand growth is also projected to slow to 5.8% year-on-year in 2026 from 18.5% in 2025, tracking a deceleration in global passenger electric vehicle (EV) sales growth to 3.9% year-on-year from 22.8% in 2025. 

On the supply side, global lithium output is expected to grow 13.2% year-on-year in 2026, led by Australia and China, with the price recovery supporting restarts of higher cost Australian capacity despite cost pressure from energy prices and a potential sulphur shortage. 

The combined share of the top three producers — Australia, China, and Chile — is expected to decline through 2035 as Argentina and Zimbabwe ramp up output, with Zimbabwe seen as a key driver of African lithium mine development in the coming years. 

For lithium-focused miners, developers, and explorers, that creates an intricate opportunity. Higher prices are improving the economics of existing operations and could potentially help advance projects. 

However, growing supply means projects will also need to show competitive costs, scale, and a clear path to market. 

### Production and development

Albemarle (NYSE:ALB) is a top global lithium producer that extracts lithium from brine pools in Chile and the US, while mining hard-rock spodumene ore in Australia. The company converts these raw materials into battery-grade lithium carbonate and lithium hydroxide for EVs.

In Q2 2026, the company’s net sales grew 31% from US$1.3 billion to US$1.7 billion, driven by higher prices in energy storage and specialties, as well as volume growth in specialties.

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) of US$858 million increased by approximately US$522 million from the prior-year quarter, primarily due to higher net sales and ongoing cost and productivity improvements.

CEO Kent Masters says the company is continuing to see resilient demand fundamentals across its core markets, including energy storage, EVs, and semiconductors. 

“We are advancing our highest value organic growth opportunities while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation and execution,” Masters says.

On the development front, Q2 Metals (TSX-V:QTWO) is advancing the Cisco Lithium Project, which is considered the fourth largest spodumene lithium deposit by tonnage globally.

Cisco, located in Québec, Canada, has a resource estimate of 295 million tonnes (Mt) @ 1.36% lithium oxide.

The company launched a 2026 summer drill program at Cisco in June, focusing on infill drilling with the aim of converting and advancing the mineral resource from inferred to indicated. Two additional rigs will be mobilised to enhance the work program in support of an inaugural preliminary economic assessment targeted for the Canadian fall of 2026.

Cisco remains open at depth and along strike, with an exploration target of a further 44–67Mt adjacent to the current resource.

### Exploration

On the exploration front, Pioneer Minerals (ASX:PMM) owns the Benham Lithium Project comprising 30 claims totalling 1,245 hectares, located in Ontario, Canada.

Results from the maiden exploration program, conducted in 2023, identified a spodumene-bearing pegmatite outcrop up to 40m long and 5m wide, as well as mineralised pegmatite outcrops suggesting primary and accessory minerals associated with highly fractionated lithium-caesium-tantalum pegmatites, with visible spodumene concentrations of up to 80%.

In 2024, field exploration discovered spodumene-bearing pegmatites which returned channel sampling results of 1m @ 4.61% lithium oxide (Li₂O), 2.1m @ 2.33% Li₂O, 2.1m @ 1.29% Li₂O.

The Root Lake Project, located in north-western Ontario, consists of 1,927 hectares across 94 contiguous claims adjoining and along-trend from Green Technology Metals’ (ASX:GT1) McCombe and Root Bay deposits.

Previous field exploration by Pioneer confirmed that over 90 pegmatite outcrops were mapped across the project. At the Red Squirrel prospect, spodumene-bearing pegmatites were identified with a best grab sample returning 2.95% Li₂O and subsequent channel sampling up to 3,530 parts per million lithium.

Brunswick Exploration (TSX-V:BRW) also owns several lithium-prospective properties in Greenland and Canada.

In Greenland, the company owns the Nuuk licence, hosted within the Ivisaartoq Greenstone Belt, as well as the Paamiut licence. 

In late June 2026, Brunswick extended the spodumene-bearing corridor at the Nuuk Project, after confirming an additional spodumene-bearing pegmatite over 3km from the original discovery zone, nearly doubling the scale and width of the mineralised system.

CEO Killian Charles says the project’s growing scale continues to support its exploration potential. 

“As lithium markets and fundamentals gain momentum, we believe that Greenland remains one of the most exciting and underexplored jurisdictions with significant critical mineral endowment globally,” Charles says.

“With first-mover advantage, Brunswick Exploration is the only company exploring for lithium in the country.”

Brunswick also owns the Mirage, Anatacau Main, and Anatacau West projects in Canada, where drilling recently began, as previously reported.

At Anatacau, drilling will extend the known spodumene pegmatite dykes and discover new ones. Meanwhile at Mirage, drilling is targeting the lateral extensions of the MR-1 and MR-4 dykes, which are considered the richest dykes to date.
